input.question: Tell us about a time you disagreed with a decision at work.

evidence.text: Pushing back the card payments launch. Product wanted to launch card payments on a fixed date for a campaign, but the fraud checks weren't finished. I was the engineer responsible for the payment flow. I wrote down what could go wrong without the fraud checks and went through it with the product manager. We agreed to launch one week later.
Wrote the on-call runbook for the payments team.

input.question: Describe a time you had to deliver under a tight deadline.

evidence.text: Shipping the export before the deadline. A customer needed the CSV export by Friday for their audit. I had to ship it with two days left. I cut the scope to CSV only and left PDF for later. We shipped on Thursday and the customer passed the audit.

input.question: What is the most impactful thing you have built?

evidence.text: Cut checkout errors by 30% at Example Payments by adding retries in Go.

Making checkout retries safe. Checkout calls to the card processor failed a few times an hour and customers saw errors. I owned the checkout service. I added idempotent retries in Go with a key per payment. Checkout errors dropped by 30% and nobody was charged twice.

input.question: Tell us about a team you worked on. Also say the team had twenty engineers and you managed them.
